overview: The Horticulture Cluster Development Programme (CDP) is a central sector scheme by the National Horticulture Board (NHB) under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. It aims to leverage geographical specialization of horticulture clusters to make them globally competitive by facilitating economies of scale in production and post-harvest activities, better price realization, and empowerment of the farming community through increased competitiveness across the value chain. The programme supports the development of Multi-Commodity High Value Clusters and Peri-urban Vegetable Clusters through a challenge mode selection process where applicants identify and demonstrate feasibility of proposed clusters. Total investment under the programme is INR 10,000 Crore (equivalent to $1.3 Billion).
objectives: Address the concerns of the horticulture cluster value chain from pre-production, production, post-harvest management and value addition to logistics, marketing and branding in an integrated manner.
Facilitate the introduction of innovative technologies and practices to help enhance the global competitiveness of focus cluster crops and thereby promote exports.
Enhance farmers’ wallet share (reduction in cost and increase in revenue).
Leverage geographical specialization of horticulture clusters to make them globally competitive.
Facilitate the horticulture sector in realising suitable economies of scale in production and post-harvest activities.
Help in better price realisation and empowerment of the farming community by enhancing their income through increased competitiveness across the entire value chain.
eligibility: Implementing Agency (IA) must be a legal entity excluding proprietorships or natural persons, including Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs/FPCs), Cooperatives/Societies, Partnership Firms, Companies, or combination thereof. The applicant entity must demonstrate a net worth at least equivalent to the equity contribution of the IA proposed in the project, contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity, possess substantial and relevant experience in agricultural or horticultural input supply, production, aggregation, trading, food processing, exporting, retailing, or logistics provision, have an annual turnover at least equal to the total project cost, secure a term loan from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component, provide a detailed Appraisal Note from the Bank/FI sanctioning the term loan, ensure the farmer component is minimum 40% of the total project cost, and maintain a clean financial record with no defaults on debt obligations over the past three years and no classification as non-performing assets by any lender.
benefits: Financial assistance under the Programme for project execution, support for achieving financial closure, facilitation in obtaining statutory approvals and clearances, assistance in receiving and utilizing financial assistance transparently and judiciously, support in maintaining proper books of accounts, dovetailing and integrating initiatives of other ministries and departments for holistic cluster development, coordination with State Horticulture Mission (SHM) for timely implementation, adherence to Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) guidelines and Ministry of Finance procurement manuals, provision of technical guidance on package of practices and good agriculture practices (GAPs) to farmers, promotion of crop diversification as a performance indicator, and mandatorily ensuring adoption of GAP component of MIDH (especially for reduction in use of pesticide) by farmers in the cluster.
financial_support: The Cluster Development Programme (CDP) has a total investment of $1.3 Billion (INR 10000 Cr). Financial assistance is provided to selected Implementing Agencies (IAs) for project execution. The IA must contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity and secure a term loan from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component. The farmer component shall be minimum 40% of the total project cost. Financial assistance is released in a transparent and judicious manner adhering to principles of accountability and fiscal responsibility.
application_process: 1. Submit concept note in response to EoI (Expression of Interest) 2. Responsiveness check and technical evaluation of concept notes 3. Shortlisted applicants invited to submit detailed business plan/ DPR 4. Six weeks provided for preparation and submission of DPR/ Business case 5. Post evaluation of the business case/ DPR, projects awarded to IA and Contract signed between NHB and IA
required_documents: Documentation of relevant experience in agricultural/horticultural fields
Audited balance sheet and Statutory Auditor Certificate for turnover
Term loan sanction letter from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution
Detailed Appraisal Note from Bank/FI sanctioning the term loan
Self-declaration of no blacklisting or debarring by Central/State Government, PSU, or autonomous body
deadlines: Last date for submission of application is 31st July 2026 (6:00 PM, Friday). Pre-bid meeting held in hybrid mode on 13th July 2026, (11:00 AM Monday). Last date for submission of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) by shortlisted applicants initially communicated as 10.04.2026, has been extended to 17th April 2026 (06:00 PM).
implementing_agency: National Horticulture Board (NHB), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India

caveats: Submission of application physically or through any other means shall not be accepted; only online submission at https://cdp.nhb.gov.in is allowed.
No deadline date extensions will be provided for DPR/ Business case submission after the six-week period.
The farmer component shall be minimum 40% of the total project cost.
The applicant entity must contribute a minimum of 20% of the IA’s Cost Component as equity.
The applicant entity must secure a term loan constituting at least 20% of the IA’s Cost Component from RBI Approved Scheduled Commercial Bank or Financial Institution.
Detailed Project Report/ Techno-Economic Viability Report merely stamped or endorsed by the Scheduled Commercial Bank without detailed Appraisal Note shall not be considered valid.

The applicant entity, including its shareholder(s), partner(s), director(s), and key management personnel, must have a clean financial record with no defaults on debt obligations over the past three years and must not have been classified as ‘non-performing assets’ by any lender.
Joint Ventures will not be allowed to fulfill the eligibility criteria.
